title_en: Sun Qingjun v. Owner's Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing — dispute over owners' right to know
ruling_gist_en: As owners of condominium units, owners have the right to be informed, and have the right to know matters related to common ownership and common management rights within the building subdivision of their residential community. The owners' committee shall fully and reasonably disclose the information and materials in its possession. The exercise of the right to be informed by owners should also be reasonably restricted to prevent abuse of rights, and its scope should be limited to information concerning the legitimate rights and interests of owners, and shall follow the principle of simplicity.

full_text_en:
Sun Qingjun v. Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community — dispute over owners’ right to information

【Ruling Summary】

As a unit owner of a condominium building, an owner has the right to information, including the right to know matters concerning the common ownership and co-management rights within the building subdivision. The owners’ committee shall fully and reasonably disclose the information and materials in its possession. The exercise of the owner’s right to information should also be reasonably restricted to prevent abuse, and its scope shall be limited to information involving the owner’s lawful rights and interests, following the principle of convenience.

Plaintiff: Sun Qingjun, male, 43 years old, residing in Gulou District, Nanjing.

Defendant: Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, domiciled at Room 101, Building 1, Yuanmengyuan, Qingjiang Huayuan, Gulou District, Nanjing.

The plaintiff, Sun Qingjun, filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community (hereinafter referred to as “Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee”), over a dispute concerning the owners’ right to information.

Plaintiff’s Allegations: The plaintiff is an owner of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community. Since the current owners’ committee took over the community in December 2012, the management has been chaotic, financial revenue and expenditure have been opaque, information that should be disclosed in accordance with the law has never been made public, and there have even been illegal acts, causing damage to the lawful rights and interests of the plaintiff and other owners. The plaintiff requested to access relevant information from the owners’ committee but was refused on various pretexts. To protect the lawful rights and interests of the owners, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting a judgment ordering: 1. The defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, to publish the following information and materials on the community bulletin board: (1) the collection and use of maintenance funds for the buildings and ancillary facilities of Qingjiang Huayuan Community; (2) all decisions, resolutions, and meeting minutes of the current owners’ committee; (3) the service contract between the current owners’ committee and the property management company, and the use and income from the common areas; (4) the revenue and expenditure allocation of parking fees and the disposition of parking spaces in the community; (5) the annual financial revenue and expenditure accounts and vouchers during the term of the current owners’ committee. 2. The litigation costs to be borne by the defendant.

Defendant’s Defense: 1. The plaintiff’s request should be exercised collectively through the owners’ meeting. However, due to conflicts between some owners and the defendant, the owners’ committee cannot convene a meeting, so the items requested by the plaintiff cannot be disclosed through the owners’ meeting. 2. Regarding the plaintiff’s request for disclosure of maintenance funds, the defendant will disclose the use of maintenance funds for the plaintiff’s unit in court. Furthermore, the use of the community’s maintenance funds should be reported to the relevant administrative authorities, and the owners’ committee does not have detailed information. 3. Regarding parking spaces, allocation is based on a first-come, first-served basis, so specific disposition details cannot be provided; the plaintiff should inquire with the community property management company. The other requests have already been disclosed by the defendant.

Facts Found by the Court:

The plaintiff, Sun Qingjun, is the owner of Room XX, Unit X, Building X, Qingfengyuan, Gulou District, Nanjing, which is located within the Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community.

On April 4, 2014, the defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, posted on the community bulletin board a “Notice on the Current Status of the Owners’ Committee’s Account Funds.” The main content was: On January 27, 2014, the owners’ committee received RMB 2,334,820 as compensation for the expropriation of land for a street-crossing passage on behalf of the community. To preserve and increase the value of public income, the owners’ committee staff used a personal account via online banking from February 26 to 28, 2014, in four transactions totaling RMB 2.6 million to purchase two money market funds. Subsequently, upon court request, the funds were redeemed on April 3, 2014, and the principal of RMB 2.6 million and the income of RMB 10,443.12 were returned to the owners’ committee’s public account. This was hereby disclosed. Subsequently, the defendant disclosed on the community bulletin board the income and expenditure of the owners’ committee for 2013 and 2014. The 2013 income and expenditure summary listed 5 income items and 5 expenditure items; the 2014 summary listed 3 income items and 4 expenditure items. On July 11, 2015, the defendant posted a notice on the community bulletin board informing all owners that information such as the change of property management and the 2014 financial revenue and expenditure accounts of the owners’ committee had been published. If owners needed further information, they were advised to inquire and review at the owners’ committee office.

It was also found that on December 14, 2012, the previous Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee signed a “Qingjiang Huayuan Community Property Service Contract” with Wuxi Xiehe Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Xiehe Company”), authorizing it to manage the community’s property. This property service contract was posted on the community bulletin board. On March 15, 2015, the defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, sent a letter to Xiehe Company urging payment of the 2014 public income. Xiehe Company replied that it would submit and disclose the 2014 public income situation before March 30, 2015, and that the specific arrears amount and settlement date would be determined after consultation with the defendant. On June 19, 2015, the defendant posted a “Notice of Property Management Change” on the community bulletin board, informing community owners that it had received notice from Xiehe Company that, due to impending bankruptcy, it recommended Jiangsu Qicheng Property Service Company (hereinafter “Qicheng Company”) to take over management. Subsequently, the defendant signed a property service contract with Qicheng Company and published the “Property Service Contract” on the community bulletin board. The plaintiff, Sun Qingjun, filed this lawsuit against the defendant for failure to disclose relevant information, requesting a judgment as prayed.

During the trial, the defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, submitted documents concerning the use of maintenance funds, including the bid opening and evaluation announcement for the roof and wall waterproofing project of Qingjiang Huayuan Community (tendering time: July 2013), the tender documents, the letter of acceptance, the consultation form for the application for use of maintenance funds, and part of the detailed apportionment. The plaintiff acknowledged these but argued that the defendant should disclose all maintenance fund information, not just the specific special maintenance fund information.

Opinion of the Court:

Owners have the right to know matters related to community public affairs and property management. They may request the owners’ committee and the property management company to disclose and provide access to information and materials that should be disclosed to owners in accordance with the law and that are actually in the possession of the owners’ committee and the property management company. As an owner, the plaintiff, Sun Qingjun, is entitled to demand that the defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, disclose the information and materials in its possession. According to Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Condominium Ownership, owners are entitled to request the disclosure of and access to the following materials: (1) the collection and use of maintenance funds for buildings and their ancillary facilities; (2) the management rules, the rules of procedure for the owners’ meeting, and the decisions and meeting minutes of the owners’ meeting or the owners’ committee; (3) the property service contract, and the use and income of the common areas; (4) the disposition of parking spaces and garages planned for parking within the building subdivision; (5) other information and materials that should be disclosed to owners. Therefore, the defendant’s defense that the plaintiff’s claimed rights should be exercised collectively through the owners’ meeting lacks legal basis, is inconsistent with the principles of economy and convenience, and is detrimental to the exercise and protection of the owners’ right to information. Hence, this defense is not upheld. The Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee shall ensure the owners’ right to inspect these materials and promptly disclose information related to the owners’ interests.

Regarding the plaintiff’s claim for disclosure of the collection and use of maintenance funds for the buildings and ancillary facilities of Qingjiang Huayuan Community: Maintenance funds for buildings and ancillary facilities are owned by the owners in common. They are used for the repair and replacement of the common parts and common facilities and equipment of the residential units after the expiration of the warranty period. Owners have the right to know how these funds are used. As the representative of all community owners, the defendant, the Qingjiang Huayuan Owners’ Committee, should be aware of the collection and use of maintenance funds. Whether or not the funds are directly controlled by the defendant does not affect its obligation to disclose the maintenance fund situation. The documents submitted by the defendant to the court regarding the use of funds for the roof and wall waterproofing project in 2013 only reflect part of the fund usage, not the entire collection and use of maintenance funds. Therefore, the plaintiff’s claim on this point is upheld. Regarding the claim for disclosure of all decisions, resolutions, and meeting minutes of the current owners’ committee: The decisions, resolutions, and meeting minutes made by the owners’ committee are closely related to the rights of owners and should be made public and available for inspection by owners. Although the defendant submitted meeting minutes and other evidence during the trial, it did not disclose them to all owners in the community. Therefore, the plaintiff’s claim on this point is upheld. Regarding the claim for disclosure of the property service contract between the current owners’ committee and the property management company, and the use and income of the common areas: The defendant has already posted on the community bulletin board the “Property Service Contracts” signed with Xiehe Company and Qicheng Company, and the plaintiff can review these contracts through the defendant’s office. Therefore, the claim for disclosure of the contract is not upheld. However, the use and income of the common areas are closely related to the interests of the owners. Although issues such as Xiehe Company’s failure to turn over public income in a timely manner exist, the defendant, as the representative of all owners, should promptly pursue recovery, protect the lawful rights and interests of the owners, and promptly disclose the current use and income situation. Regarding the claim for disclosure of the revenue and expenditure allocation of parking fees and the disposition of parking spaces in the community: Community parking spaces that are common areas (i.e., spaces outside planned areas), although managed by the property management company on behalf, are owned by all owners in common. Owners have the right to know the revenue and expenditure allocation of parking fees for the common areas and the disposition of parking spaces. The defendant should promptly contact the property management company to disclose the above information. Therefore, the plaintiff’s claim on this point is upheld. Regarding the claim for disclosure of the annual financial revenue and expenditure accounts and vouchers during the term of the current owners’ committee: The community’s financial revenue and expenditure are closely related to the specific interests of the owners, and the owners’ committee should disclose them. Although the defendant posted summary tables of income and expenditure for 2013 and 2014 on the community bulletin board, the items listed were few and not sufficiently detailed. Although the defendant later submitted detailed account statements and vouchers during the trial, it did not fulfill its obligation to disclose them. Therefore, the plaintiff’s claim on this point is upheld.

In summary, in accordance with Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Condominium Ownership, Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Gulou District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, rendered the following judgment on September 16, 2015:

1. The defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, shall, within thirty days of this judgment taking effect, post on the community bulletin board or in public areas of the community the collection and use of maintenance funds for the buildings and ancillary facilities of Qingjiang Huayuan Community since the establishment of the current owners’ committee.

2. The defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, shall, within thirty days of this judgment taking effect, post on the community bulletin board or in public areas of the community the decisions, resolutions, and meeting minutes of the owners’ committee since the establishment of the current owners’ committee.

3. The defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, shall, within thirty days of this judgment taking effect, post on the community bulletin board or in public areas of the community the use and income of the common areas of Qingjiang Huayuan Community (at least semi-annually) since the establishment of the current owners’ committee.

4. The defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, shall, within thirty days of this judgment taking effect, post on the community bulletin board or in public areas of the community the revenue and expenditure allocation of parking fees and the disposition of parking spaces in Qingjiang Huayuan Community since the establishment of the current owners’ committee.

5. The defendant, the Owners’ Committee of Qingjiang Huayuan Residential Community, Nanjing, shall, within thirty days of this judgment taking effect, post on the community bulletin board or in public areas of the community the detailed annual financial revenue and expenditure accounts and vouchers since the establishment of the current owners’ committee.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
